headline: AI Mindmeld uses independently trained connectors to pass scientific representations into frozen LLMs
summary: A 21 October arXiv preprint introduces the Latent Interconnect Protocol (LIP), which maps representations from scientific specialist models into selected internal states of a shared frozen language model. The authors demonstrate separate connectors for three protein and three molecule specialists with Gemma 3 4B/12B and Kimi K2.6; they report reuse across question types and combining independently trained connectors without joint training. Reported results include held-out-object performance, transfer to some unseen tasks and cross-specialist composition. The same paper reports molecule-task negative transfer after connector training, reduced protein-property performance when extended reasoning is requested, and cases where the LLM misreads latent inputs. This is a paper-reported architecture demonstration, not independent evidence of reliable general scientific reasoning or an end-to-end scientific workflow benefit.
